name: AFM level 2 task 9: Friction Repeatability And Surface-Check Measurement
description: Acquire exactly three consecutive contact-mode lateral-force images of the same region without changing any acquisition parameter. Use a scan size of $\pu{5 µm} \times \pu{5 µm}$, resolution of $256 \times 256$ pixels, time per line of 0.075 s, setpoint of 0.1 V, and P/I/D gains of 100/50/0. For every acquisition, calculate average friction magnitude from the lateral channels, and calculate rms and average roughness from the height channel. Report all roughness values in nanometres ($\pu{nm}$). Report all friction-signal values, in volts ($\pu{V}$) from the lateral channel.
submission_format: {"rms_roughness_1": "<numerical_value without units>", "mean_roughness_1": "<numerical_value without units>", "average_friction_1": "<numerical_value without units>", "path_1": "<absolute_path_to_raw_nid_image>", "rms_roughness_2": "<numerical_value without units>", "mean_roughness_2": "<numerical_value without units>", "average_friction_2": "<numerical_value without units>", "path_2": "<absolute_path_to_raw_nid_image>", "rms_roughness_3": "<numerical_value without units>", "mean_roughness_3": "<numerical_value without units>", "average_friction_3": "<numerical_value without units>", "path_3": "<absolute_path_to_raw_nid_image>"} e.g. {"rms_roughness_1": "42.78", "mean_roughness_1": "34.20", "average_friction_1": "0.12", "path_1": "/results/afm_images/image1.nid", "rms_roughness_2": "38.55", "mean_roughness_2": "30.00", "average_friction_2": "0.15", "path_2": "/results/afm_images/image2.nid", "rms_roughness_3": "40.12", "mean_roughness_3": "32.10", "average_friction_3": "0.18", "path_3": "/results/afm_images/image3.nid"} Return one JSON object. Example values are illustrative, not target answers. Suffixes _1, _2, and _3 identify the first, second, and third acquisitions in the order specified in the question; use a separate raw .nid file for each. Enter numerical values without unit text, using the units specified in the question. mean_roughness denotes the average absolute height deviation from the mean height. Roughness values must be in nm (convert metre-valued height data by multiplying by 1e9). Friction-signal values must be in V, not N.
